propositions: The autouse _no_repo_commits guard invokes git rev-parse HEAD before and after every test, consuming ~207 runner-seconds and ~75 wall-seconds on the full 13k-test suite (9.3% of wall time on macOS).

Current implementation uses two per-test Git subprocesses and lacks in-process HEAD fingerprinting; eliminating these calls requires either adding a Git library dependency, hand-parsing ref storage, or weakening the per-test checkout attribution contract.

Four major OSS projects (pytest, pip, Poetry, pre-commit) achieve repo isolation by creating mutable state in temporary directories rather than running source-checkout Git subprocesses in per-test hot paths, establishing consensus against this pattern.

No fidelity-preserving primitive meets both the session attribution guard requirement (detecting which test moved HEAD) and the automatic-approval bar without adding library dependencies or unsafe custom ref parsing.
Candidate implementation measured ~75s projected macOS wall-time saving and ~207 runner-second reduction but is blocked pending explicit operator design choice or new safe primitive evidence.
